paragraphs: Yehudah: Abba bar Yehudah; Isi bar Yehudah; Rabbi Elazar ben Yehudah; Dostai ben Yehudah; Rav Huna ben Yehudah; Rabbi Chiyya ben Yehudah; Chana, or Chinena, or Chananyah ben Yehudah; Mattityah ben Yehudah; Rabbi Sama ben Yehudah; Rabbi Shmuel ben Yehudah; Rabbi Tanchum ben Yehudah. [Glosses: Yehudah. (1) Bava Kamma 19b, beginning: ‘Rabbi Yehudah Nesia and Rabbi Oshaya were sitting in Rabbi Yehudah’s courtyard.’ It should read ‘in Rav Yehudah’s courtyard’; in the new Talmud edition this was not corrected. (2) Chullin 45b: ‘Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak came before Rabbi Yehudah’ should read ‘Rav Yehudah’; it was not corrected. (3) Zevachim 11a and 13b: ‘Rabbi Yehudah be-Rabbi Chiyya’—the title Rabbi is superfluous; it was not corrected. [The checked 11a reads Rav Yehudah, and 13b reads Rabbi Yehudah.] In Chullin 105b, ‘Rav Yehudah be-Rav Chiyya’ should read ‘Yehudah be-Rabbi Chiyya.’ But that matter at the end of the first chapter of Eruvin, 47b, has ‘Rabbi Chiyya bar Ashi said.’ [The parallel on final waters is at 17b in the checked text, which reads Rav Chiyya bar Ashi.] In Eruvin 103b, ‘Rav Yehudah be-Rabbi Chiyya,’ Rav is superfluous, since he was not ordained; it was not corrected. (4) Sanhedrin 6b: ‘Rabbi Yehudah ben Korchah’ should read ‘Yehoshua’; so it appears in Ein Yaakov and Yalkut, Zechariah, section 8, and so is implied by the Gemara at the bottom of the page. (5) Bava Batra 144a: ‘Rabbi Yehudah and Rav Pappi’ should read ‘Rav Yehudah.’ (6) Taanit 3b: ‘Ulla, and some say Rabbi Yehudah’ should read ‘Rav Yehudah’; so it appears in Rashi, but it was not corrected. (7) Yoma 78a: ‘Yehudah bar Gerogeret’—it seems to me that the word bar is a scribal error; it was not corrected. [The checked text retains bar and reads Gerogerot.] (8) Shabbat 126a–b: ‘Rav Yehudah bar Shilat’; in several places, Shila. In the new Talmud edition, page a has Shilat, and page b has Shila twice. (9) Yevamot 94a, end: ‘Rabbi Yehudah said in Rav’s name’ should read ‘Rav Yehudah.’ (10) Shabbat 153a and Eruvin 14b, end: ‘Rabbi Yehudah be-Rav Shmuel bar Shila’; in several places, Shilat. It was not corrected. [The checked Shabbat reads Rav Yehudah son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat. The checked Eruvin has the same form with bar Shilat in brackets.] (11) Shabbat 57b: ‘Rav Yehudah in Abaye’s name.’ This requires examination, for Abaye married the daughter of Rav Yehudah’s grandson; perhaps this is an earlier Abaye. It was not corrected. (12) Pesachim 27a: ‘Rav Yehudah said: Rav Yosef said: Shmuel said.’ This requires examination, for Rav Yosef was Rav Yehudah’s student, and Rav Yehudah was Shmuel’s student. It seems to me that it should read ‘Rav Yosef said: Rav Yehudah said: Shmuel said.’ It was not corrected. [The checked text has the order proposed by the glossator.] (13) Pesachim 92b, beginning: ‘Rav Yehudah bar Abaye.’ This requires examination, for he is not found elsewhere; in the new Talmud edition an alternative reading is Ammi. (14) Berakhot 19b: ‘Yehudah bar Ashi’; perhaps it should read ‘bar Ammi.’ It was not corrected. (15) Menachot 26b: in the new Talmud edition, ‘Rabbi Yehudah said to Rabbah bar Rav Yitzchak, I shall explain it to you’ should read ‘Rav Yehudah.’ (16) Shabbat 130b: ‘Resh Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi’; perhaps it should read ‘Rabbi Yehudah Nesia.’ It was not corrected.]
